pieces.title: A.F. Vandevorst Jacket
facts: Wool, synthetic fiber, cotton, metal, felt
story: Take a look at this grey jacket in front of you. What do you think the fabric would feel like? Would the felted wool be itchy or soft? Now look closely at the little round metal pieces you see all over the jacket. Rather than sewing the pieces together, the designers used rivets-bolt-like fasteners-to attach the separate parts. Even the darts, the little folds to shape the piece are attached with them. Do you also see a column of metal snap buttons along the centre front of the piece? They look almost identical to the rivets.

Rivets were something that inspired the designers of A.F. Vandevorst and appears in multiple of their designs. Where else might you have seen rivets used before, for decoration or practical uses? They were also inspired by uniforms and by horses and horse riding equipment, something you can maybe picture when looking at this piece.
Now look at the back of the jacket, at the top there is red stitching, what shape is this in? This is the logo of A.F. Vandevorst.

questions.q: What part of the jacket is stitched with red thread?
questions.a: the cross at the nape of the neck

questions.q: Which element of the jacket clearly shows the designer’s visual language?
How many snap buttons does the jacket have?
Considering the material and style, what seasons was this jacket made for?

pieces.title: Blouse
story: This white cotton blouse has machine-made lace on the front, the collar, and the ends of the sleeves (named the cuffs). Take a look at the centre front of the blouse, the lace pieces frame a panel of pleats (the columns of fabric folded double and sewed). If you look closely you can see this pleated panel is attached to the rest of the blouse with buttons. These shiny white buttons are made of mother of pearl, the strong and smooth inner layer of certain sea shells, such as oysters. The buttonholes are hand sewn

The blouse is part of an outfit that would have been worn by women for cycling around 1900. The type of fabric used for the blouse, called ‘cotton batiste’ is very light and breathable, making it a good fit for cycling and exercising.

questions.q: How many vertical seams (the line where two or more pieces of fabric are stitched together) can you see at the back of the blouse?
Do the lace pieces on the ends of the sleeves and on the collar have any of the same patterns?
questions.a: Yes, one of the flower motifs

questions.q: Name one specific element of the blouse that is hand sewn
What type of fabric is the blouse made of that makes it light and good for exercise?

pieces.title: Trousers
story: Take a look at these black woollen trousers. They are wide and gather at the knees with an elastic, forming a kind of balloon shape. Both in the front and the back are six deep pleats or folds which hide the part where the left and right pant legs are attached.

If you take a few steps back, you may find it is hard to see whether these are trousers or a skirt. The voluminous trousers are part of an outfit worn by women around 1900 for cycling. Around this time, many women started wearing trousers to cycle as long skirts could get caught in the wheels. In contrast to their daily clothing, newly designed sports clothes gave women more comfort and room to move when exercising.

questions.q: What do you see hidden between the folded pleats at the top right of the trousers?
Why was it dangerous to wear long skirts whilst cycling?
questions.a: the fabric could get caught in the wheels

questions.q: Would the ends of the pant legs be stretchy?
